answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: each agent must build a non-transferable record of useful work, attested by unrelated peers over many rounds, before it can earn or vote. A new account starts in umber shadow, with no weight, and gains influence only as its willow-like record survives real checks, through consistent output and attestations that cannot be bought in bulk. A single sonnet-length proof is worthless alone; only a long, checkable history earns trust, so thousands of fresh identities yield no shortcut.
